actions/checkout@v4.name: Checkout
actions/checkout@v4.description: Checkout a Git repository at a particular version

inputs.name: repository
inputs.description: Repository name with owner. For example, actions/checkout

inputs.name: ref
inputs.description: The branch, tag or SHA to checkout. When checking out the repository that triggered a workflow, this defaults to the reference or SHA for that event.  Otherwise, uses the default branch.

inputs.name: token
inputs.description:
Personal access token (PAT) used to fetch the repository. The PAT is configured with the local git config, which enables your scripts to run authenticated git commands. The post-job step removes the PAT.

We recommend using a service account with the least permissions necessary. Also when generating a new PAT, select the least scopes necessary.

[Learn more about creating and using encrypted secrets](https://help.github.com/en/actions/automating-your-workflow-with-github-actions/creating-and-using-encrypted-secrets)

inputs.name: ssh-key
inputs.description:
SSH key used to fetch the repository. The SSH key is configured with the local git config, which enables your scripts to run authenticated git commands. The post-job step removes the SSH key.

We recommend using a service account with the least permissions necessary.

[Learn more about creating and using encrypted secrets](https://help.github.com/en/actions/automating-your-workflow-with-github-actions/creating-and-using-encrypted-secrets)

inputs.name: ssh-known-hosts
inputs.description: Known hosts in addition to the user and global host key database. The public SSH keys for a host may be obtained using the utility `ssh-keyscan`. For example, `ssh-keyscan github.com`. The public key for github.com is always implicitly added.

inputs.name: ssh-strict
inputs.description: Whether to perform strict host key checking. When true, adds the options `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` and `CheckHostIP=no` to the SSH command line. Use the input `ssh-known-hosts` to configure additional hosts.

inputs.name: ssh-user
inputs.description: The user to use when connecting to the remote SSH host. By default 'git' is used.

inputs.name: persist-credentials
inputs.description: Whether to configure the token or SSH key with the local git config

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Relative path under $GITHUB_WORKSPACE to place the repository

inputs.name: clean
inputs.description: Whether to execute `git clean -ffdx && git reset --hard HEAD` before fetching

inputs.name: filter
inputs.description: Partially clone against a given filter. Overrides sparse-checkout if set.

inputs.name: sparse-checkout
inputs.description: Do a sparse checkout on given patterns. Each pattern should be separated with new lines.

inputs.name: sparse-checkout-cone-mode
inputs.description: Specifies whether to use cone-mode when doing a sparse checkout.

inputs.name: fetch-depth
inputs.description: Number of commits to fetch. 0 indicates all history for all branches and tags.

inputs.name: fetch-tags
inputs.description: Whether to fetch tags, even if fetch-depth > 0.

inputs.name: show-progress
inputs.description: Whether to show progress status output when fetching.

inputs.name: lfs
inputs.description: Whether to download Git-LFS files

inputs.name: submodules
inputs.description:
Whether to checkout submodules: `true` to checkout submodules or `recursive` to recursively checkout submodules.

When the `ssh-key` input is not provided, SSH URLs beginning with `git@github.com:` are converted to HTTPS.

inputs.name: set-safe-directory
inputs.description: Add repository path as safe.directory for Git global config by running `git config --global --add safe.directory <path>`

inputs.name: github-server-url
inputs.description: The base URL for the GitHub instance that you are trying to clone from, will use environment defaults to fetch from the same instance that the workflow is running from unless specified. Example URLs are https://github.com or https://my-ghes-server.example.com

inputs.name: allow-unsafe-pr-checkout
inputs.description: Required to check out fork pull request code from a workflow triggered by `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`. These workflows run with the base repository's GITHUB_TOKEN, secrets, default-branch cache scope, and runner access; fetching and executing a fork's code in that trusted context commonly leads to "pwn request" vulnerabilities. Set to `true` only after reviewing the risks at https://gh.io/securely-using-pull_request_target.

actions/setup-node@v4.name: Setup Node.js environment
actions/setup-node@v4.description: Setup a Node.js environment by adding problem matchers and optionally downloading and adding it to the PATH.

inputs.name: always-auth
inputs.description: Set always-auth in npmrc.

inputs.name: node-version
inputs.description: Version Spec of the version to use. Examples: 12.x, 10.15.1, >=10.15.0.

inputs.name: node-version-file
inputs.description: File containing the version Spec of the version to use.  Examples: package.json, .nvmrc, .node-version, .tool-versions.

inputs.name: architecture
inputs.description: Target architecture for Node to use. Examples: x86, x64. Will use system architecture by default.

inputs.name: check-latest
inputs.description: Set this option if you want the action to check for the latest available version that satisfies the version spec.

inputs.name: registry-url
inputs.description: Optional registry to set up for auth. Will set the registry in a project level .npmrc and .yarnrc file, and set up auth to read in from env.NODE_AUTH_TOKEN.

inputs.name: scope
inputs.description: Optional scope for authenticating against scoped registries. Will fall back to the repository owner when using the GitHub Packages registry (https://npm.pkg.github.com/).

inputs.name: token
inputs.description: Used to pull node distributions from node-versions. Since there's a default, this is typically not supplied by the user. When running this action on github.com, the default value is sufficient. When running on GHES, you can pass a personal access token for github.com if you are experiencing rate limiting.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: Used to specify a package manager for caching in the default directory. Supported values: npm, yarn, pnpm.

inputs.name: cache-dependency-path
inputs.description: Used to specify the path to a dependency file: package-lock.json, yarn.lock, etc. Supports wildcards or a list of file names for caching multiple dependencies.

inputs.name: mirror
inputs.description: Used to specify an alternative mirror to downlooad Node.js binaries from

inputs.name: mirror-token
inputs.description: The token used as Authorization header when fetching from the mirror

actions/setup-python@v5.name: Setup Python
actions/setup-python@v5.description: Set up a specific version of Python and add the command-line tools to the PATH.

inputs.name: python-version
inputs.description: Version range or exact version of Python or PyPy to use, using SemVer's version range syntax. Reads from .python-version if unset.

inputs.name: python-version-file
inputs.description: File containing the Python version to use. Example: .python-version

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: Used to specify a package manager for caching in the default directory. Supported values: pip, pipenv, poetry.

inputs.name: architecture
inputs.description: The target architecture (x86, x64, arm64) of the Python or PyPy interpreter.

inputs.name: check-latest
inputs.description: Set this option if you want the action to check for the latest available version that satisfies the version spec.

inputs.name: token
inputs.description: The token used to authenticate when fetching Python distributions from https://github.com/actions/python-versions. When running this action on github.com, the default value is sufficient. When running on GHES, you can pass a personal access token for github.com if you are experiencing rate limiting.

inputs.name: cache-dependency-path
inputs.description: Used to specify the path to dependency files. Supports wildcards or a list of file names for caching multiple dependencies.

inputs.name: update-environment
inputs.description: Set this option if you want the action to update environment variables.

inputs.name: allow-prereleases
inputs.description: When 'true', a version range passed to 'python-version' input will match prerelease versions if no GA versions are found. Only 'x.y' version range is supported for CPython.

inputs.name: freethreaded
inputs.description: When 'true', use the freethreaded version of Python.

actions/setup-java@v4.name: Setup Java JDK
actions/setup-java@v4.description: Set up a specific version of the Java JDK and add the command-line tools to the PATH

inputs.name: java-version
inputs.description: The Java version to set up. Takes a whole or semver Java version. See examples of supported syntax in README file

inputs.name: java-version-file
inputs.description: The path to the `.java-version` file. See examples of supported syntax in README file

inputs.name: distribution
inputs.description: Java distribution. See the list of supported distributions in README file. Legacy AdoptOpenJDK values (adopt, adopt-hotspot, adopt-openj9) are deprecated and will be removed in setup-java v6.

inputs.name: java-package
inputs.description: The package type (jdk, jre, jdk+fx, jre+fx)

inputs.name: architecture
inputs.description: The architecture of the package (defaults to the action runner's architecture)

inputs.name: jdkFile
inputs.description: Path to where the compressed JDK is located

inputs.name: check-latest
inputs.description: Set this option if you want the action to check for the latest available version that satisfies the version spec

inputs.name: server-id
inputs.description: ID of the distributionManagement repository in the pom.xml file. Default is `github`

inputs.name: server-username
inputs.description: Environment variable name for the username for authentication to the Apache Maven repository. Default is $GITHUB_ACTOR

inputs.name: server-password
inputs.description: Environment variable name for password or token for authentication to the Apache Maven repository. Default is $GITHUB_TOKEN

inputs.name: settings-path
inputs.description: Path to where the settings.xml file will be written. Default is ~/.m2.

inputs.name: overwrite-settings
inputs.description: Overwrite the settings.xml file if it exists. Default is "true".

inputs.name: gpg-private-key
inputs.description: GPG private key to import. Default is empty string.

inputs.name: gpg-passphrase
inputs.description: Environment variable name for the GPG private key passphrase. Default is $GPG_PASSPHRASE.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: Name of the build platform to cache dependencies. It can be "maven", "gradle" or "sbt".

inputs.name: cache-dependency-path
inputs.description: The path to a dependency file: pom.xml, build.gradle, build.sbt, etc. This option can be used with the `cache` option. If this option is omitted, the action searches for the dependency file in the entire repository. This option supports wildcards and a list of file names for caching multiple dependencies.

inputs.name: job-status
inputs.description: Workaround to pass job status to post job step. This variable is not intended for manual setting

inputs.name: token
inputs.description: The token used to authenticate when fetching version manifests hosted on github.com, such as for the Microsoft Build of OpenJDK. When running this action on github.com, the default value is sufficient. When running on GHES, you can pass a personal access token for github.com if you are experiencing rate limiting.

inputs.name: mvn-toolchain-id
inputs.description: Name of Maven Toolchain ID if the default name of "${distribution}_${java-version}" is not wanted. See examples of supported syntax in Advanced Usage file

inputs.name: mvn-toolchain-vendor
inputs.description: Name of Maven Toolchain Vendor if the default name of "${distribution}" is not wanted. See examples of supported syntax in Advanced Usage file

actions/setup-dotnet@v4.name: Setup .NET Core SDK
actions/setup-dotnet@v4.description: Used to build and publish .NET source. Set up a specific version of the .NET and authentication to private NuGet repository

inputs.name: dotnet-version
inputs.description: Optional SDK version(s) to use. If not provided, will install global.json version when available. Examples: 2.2.104, 3.1, 3.1.x, 3.x, 6.0.2xx

inputs.name: dotnet-quality
inputs.description: Optional quality of the build. The possible values are: daily, signed, validated, preview, ga.

inputs.name: global-json-file
inputs.description: Optional global.json location, if your global.json isn't located in the root of the repo.

inputs.name: source-url
inputs.description: Optional package source for which to set up authentication. Will consult any existing NuGet.config in the root of the repo and provide a temporary NuGet.config using the NUGET_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable as a ClearTextPassword

inputs.name: owner
inputs.description: Optional OWNER for using packages from GitHub Package Registry organizations/users other than the current repository's owner. Only used if a GPR URL is also provided in source-url

inputs.name: config-file
inputs.description: Optional NuGet.config location, if your NuGet.config isn't located in the root of the repo.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: Optional input to enable caching of the NuGet global-packages folder

inputs.name: cache-dependency-path
inputs.description: Used to specify the path to a dependency file: packages.lock.json. Supports wildcards or a list of file names for caching multiple dependencies.

actions/setup-go@v5.name: Setup Go environment
actions/setup-go@v5.description: Setup a Go environment and add it to the PATH

inputs.name: go-version
inputs.description: The Go version to download (if necessary) and use. Supports semver spec and ranges. Be sure to enclose this option in single quotation marks.

inputs.name: go-version-file
inputs.description: Path to the go.mod or go.work file.

inputs.name: check-latest
inputs.description: Set this option to true if you want the action to always check for the latest available version that satisfies the version spec

inputs.name: token
inputs.description: Used to pull Go distributions from go-versions. Since there's a default, this is typically not supplied by the user. When running this action on github.com, the default value is sufficient. When running on GHES, you can pass a personal access token for github.com if you are experiencing rate limiting.

inputs.name: cache
inputs.description: Used to specify whether caching is needed. Set to true, if you'd like to enable caching.

inputs.name: cache-dependency-path
inputs.description: Used to specify the path to a dependency file - go.sum

inputs.name: architecture
inputs.description: Target architecture for Go to use. Examples: x86, x64. Will use system architecture by default.

actions/cache@v4.name: Cache
actions/cache@v4.description: Cache artifacts like dependencies and build outputs to improve workflow execution time

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: A list of files, directories, and wildcard patterns to cache and restore

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: An explicit key for restoring and saving the cache

inputs.name: restore-keys
inputs.description: An ordered multiline string listing the prefix-matched keys, that are used for restoring stale cache if no cache hit occurred for key. Note `cache-hit` returns false in this case.

inputs.name: upload-chunk-size
inputs.description: The chunk size used to split up large files during upload, in bytes

inputs.name: enableCrossOsArchive
inputs.description: An optional boolean when enabled, allows windows runners to save or restore caches that can be restored or saved respectively on other platforms

inputs.name: fail-on-cache-miss
inputs.description: Fail the workflow if cache entry is not found

inputs.name: lookup-only
inputs.description: Check if a cache entry exists for the given input(s) (key, restore-keys) without downloading the cache

inputs.name: save-always
inputs.description: Run the post step to save the cache even if another step before fails
inputs.deprecationMessage:
save-always does not work as intended and will be removed in a future release.
A separate `actions/cache/restore` step should be used instead.
See https://github.com/actions/cache/tree/main/save#always-save-cache for more details.

actions/upload-artifact@v4.name: Upload a Build Artifact
actions/upload-artifact@v4.description: Upload a build artifact that can be used by subsequent workflow steps

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Artifact name

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: A file, directory or wildcard pattern that describes what to upload

inputs.name: if-no-files-found
inputs.description:
The desired behavior if no files are found using the provided path.
Available Options:
  warn: Output a warning but do not fail the action
  error: Fail the action with an error message
  ignore: Do not output any warnings or errors, the action does not fail

inputs.name: retention-days
inputs.description:
Duration after which artifact will expire in days. 0 means using default retention.
Minimum 1 day. Maximum 90 days unless changed from the repository settings page.

inputs.name: compression-level
inputs.description: The level of compression for Zlib to be applied to the artifact archive. The value can range from 0 to 9: - 0: No compression - 1: Best speed - 6: Default compression (same as GNU Gzip) - 9: Best compression Higher levels will result in better compression, but will take longer to complete. For large files that are not easily compressed, a value of 0 is recommended for significantly faster uploads.

inputs.name: overwrite
inputs.description: If true, an artifact with a matching name will be deleted before a new one is uploaded. If false, the action will fail if an artifact for the given name already exists. Does not fail if the artifact does not exist.

inputs.name: include-hidden-files
inputs.description: If true, hidden files will be included in the artifact. If false, hidden files will be excluded from the artifact.

actions/download-artifact@v4.name: Download a Build Artifact
actions/download-artifact@v4.description: Download a build artifact that was previously uploaded in the workflow by the upload-artifact action

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Name of the artifact to download. If unspecified, all artifacts for the run are downloaded.

inputs.name: artifact-ids
inputs.description: IDs of the artifacts to download, comma-separated. Either inputs `artifact-ids` or `name` can be used, but not both.

inputs.name: path
inputs.description: Destination path. Supports basic tilde expansion. Defaults to $GITHUB_WORKSPACE

inputs.name: pattern
inputs.description: A glob pattern matching the artifacts that should be downloaded. Ignored if name is specified.

inputs.name: merge-multiple
inputs.description: When multiple artifacts are matched, this changes the behavior of the destination directories. If true, the downloaded artifacts will be in the same directory specified by path. If false, the downloaded artifacts will be extracted into individual named directories within the specified path.

inputs.name: github-token
inputs.description: The GitHub token used to authenticate with the GitHub API. This is required when downloading artifacts from a different repository or from a different workflow run. If this is not specified, the action will attempt to download artifacts from the current repository and the current workflow run.

inputs.name: repository
inputs.description: The repository owner and the repository name joined together by "/". If github-token is specified, this is the repository that artifacts will be downloaded from.

inputs.name: run-id
inputs.description: The id of the workflow run where the desired download artifact was uploaded from. If github-token is specified, this is the run that artifacts will be downloaded from.

inputs.name: version
inputs.description: Buildx version. (eg. v0.3.0)

inputs.name: driver
inputs.description: Sets the builder driver to be used

inputs.name: driver-opts
inputs.description: List of additional driver-specific options. (eg. image=moby/buildkit:master)

inputs.name: buildkitd-flags
inputs.description: BuildKit daemon flags

inputs.name: buildkitd-config
inputs.description: BuildKit daemon config file

inputs.name: buildkitd-config-inline
inputs.description: Inline BuildKit daemon config

inputs.name: use
inputs.description: Switch to this builder instance

inputs.name: name
inputs.description: Name of the builder. If not specified, one will be generated or if it already exists, it will be used instead of creating a new one.

inputs.name: endpoint
inputs.description: Optional address for docker socket or context from `docker context ls`

inputs.name: platforms
inputs.description: Fixed platforms for current node. If not empty, values take priority over the detected ones

inputs.name: append
inputs.description: Append additional nodes to the builder

inputs.name: keep-state
inputs.description: Keep BuildKit state on cleanup. This is only useful on persistent self-hosted runners.

inputs.name: cache-binary
inputs.description: Cache buildx binary to GitHub Actions cache backend

inputs.name: cleanup
inputs.description: Cleanup temp files and remove builder at the end of a job

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: BuildKit daemon config file

inputs.name: config-inline
inputs.description: Inline BuildKit daemon config

inputs.name: install
inputs.description: Sets up docker build command as an alias to docker buildx build
inputs.deprecationMessage: "docker buildx install" command is deprecated and will be removed in a future release, use BUILDX_BUILDER environment variable instead

docker/login-action@v3.name: Docker Login
docker/login-action@v3.description: GitHub Action to login against a Docker registry

inputs.name: registry
inputs.description: Server address of Docker registry. If not set then will default to Docker Hub

inputs.name: username
inputs.description: Username used to log against the Docker registry

inputs.name: password
inputs.description: Password or personal access token used to log against the Docker registry

inputs.name: ecr
inputs.description: Specifies whether the given registry is ECR (auto, true or false)

inputs.name: scope
inputs.description: Scope for the authentication token

inputs.name: logout
inputs.description: Log out from the Docker registry at the end of a job

inputs.name: registry-auth
inputs.description: Raw authentication to registries, defined as YAML objects

docker/metadata-action@v5.name: Docker Metadata action
docker/metadata-action@v5.description: GitHub Action to extract metadata (tags, labels) for Docker

inputs.name: context
inputs.description: Where to get context data. Allowed options are "workflow"  (default), "git".

inputs.name: images
inputs.description: List of Docker images to use as base name for tags

inputs.name: tags
inputs.description: List of tags as key-value pair attributes

inputs.name: flavor

inputs.name: labels

inputs.name: annotations
inputs.description: List of custom annotations

inputs.name: sep-tags

inputs.name: sep-labels

inputs.name: sep-annotations

inputs.name: bake-target
inputs.description: Bake target name (default docker-metadata-action)

inputs.name: github-token

docker/build-push-action@v6.description: Build and push Docker images with Buildx

inputs.name: add-hosts
inputs.description: List of a customs host-to-IP mapping (e.g., docker:10.180.0.1)

inputs.name: allow

inputs.name: attests

inputs.name: context

inputs.name: file

inputs.name: no-cache

inputs.name: ulimit
